step1_analysis.description: A switched-capacitor amplifier stage used in pipelined ADCs to compute and amplify the residue voltage for the subsequent stage. It uses an operational amplifier, sampling/feedback capacitors, and switches.

opamp_dc_gain.description: Open-loop DC gain of the core amplifier

sky130_expected.calculation: Modeled directly in the macro-model to match the paper's 56.7 dB (approx 683 V/V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper explicitly reports 56.7 dB for the op-amp gain. The macro-model is tuned to this exact value.

opamp_gbw.description: Unity-gain bandwidth of the core amplifier

sky130_expected.calculation: Modeled directly in the macro-model to match the paper's 1.1 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper explicitly reports 1.1 GHz for the op-amp GBW. The macro-model RC time constant is set to achieve this.

closed_loop_gain.description: Closed-loop AC gain of the MDAC stage

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the capacitor ratio in the netlist. Since both are 2c, the ideal gain is 0 dB.

closed_loop_bw.description: Closed-loop -3dB bandwidth of the MDAC stage

sky130_expected.calculation: Feedback factor beta = C2B / (C1B + C2B + C3) = 2c / 6c = 1/3. Closed-loop BW = GBW * beta = 1.1 GHz / 3 = 366 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Derived from the open-loop GBW and the capacitive feedback factor.

settling_time.description: Time required for the output to settle to 1% of its final value during a step response

sky130_expected.calculation: Time constant tau = 1 / (2 * pi * BW) = 1 / (2 * pi * 366 MHz) = 435 ps. Settling to 1% takes approx 4.6 * tau = 2 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Required to support the 200 MS/s sampling rate (5 ns period, 2.5 ns half-period for settling).

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the closed-loop AC response and transient step response of the MDAC macro-model.
step3_testbench.spice:
* MDAC Stage Testbench

.param c=1p

* Macro-model for the Op-Amp (Tuned to 56.7dB DC Gain, 1.1GHz GBW)
.subckt amplifier out in_p in_n
G1 0 int_node in_p in_n 1m
R1 int_node 0 683k
C1 int_node 0 0.145p
E1 out 0 int_node 0 1
.ends

* Macro-model for the Ideal Switch
.subckt switch_ideal n1 n2
R1 n1 n2 10
.ends

* --- DUT (Modified slightly to use valid ngspice subcircuit prefixes 'X') ---
XA2c V3C 0 NET1 amplifier
Xphi1 V3C NET2 switch_ideal
C1 NET2 0 1p
C3_2c VCMO NET1 {2*c}
C1B_2c VR_XD2 NET1 {2*c}
C2B_2c NET1 V3C {2*c}
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

* DC Biasing and Stimulus
* VCMO is set to 0V for simplicity in observing the step response
VVCMO VCMO 0 0
* Input steps from 0V to 0.1V
VVR_XD2 VR_XD2 0 dc 0 ac 1 pulse(0 0.1 1n 10p 10p 10n 20n)

* Large resistor to provide DC feedback and set the operating point (prevents floating node NET1)
Rfb NET1 V3C 1G

.control
* 1. AC Analysis for Closed-Loop Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 100 1M 10G
let gain_db = vdb(V3C)
meas ac cl_gain_db find gain_db at=1M
let gain_ref = cl_gain_db - 3
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=gain_ref fall=1

* 2. Transient Analysis for Step Response and Settling Time
tran 10p 20n
* Measure final settled voltage
meas tran v_final find v(V3C) at=10n
* Measure 1% settling time (Target is -0.099V since input is 0.1V and gain is -1)
meas tran t_settle trig v(VR_XD2) val=0.05 rise=1 targ v(V3C) val=-0.099 fall=1

quit
.endc
.end
